column1: # SHIPPED-NOTE CONNECTION FIXTURE (harbor#173) — read by tests/hooks/inject-notes-test.sh.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. hooks/injection-rule/engine.test.sh proves the ENGINE works, against
# packs it writes itself. Nothing proved the packs harbor actually SHIPS were
# reachable by it. Measured 2026-08-29: of the 17 tracked notes, 14 appeared
# nowhere in any suite, and one of them — the `<tool> --full-refresh` note, which
# guards 2.5 years of history — was not installed on the box at all. A green
# suite said nothing about either, because the suite tested a different pack.
# EVERY TRACKED NOTE NEEDS A ROW, and the suite fails if one is missing. That is
# the mechanism: adding a pack with no probe cannot pass. An exemption is a row
# in the EXEMPT block of the suite with a written reason, never a silent absence.
# CORE'S PACKS ONLY. The packs that name a repo or a client live in the private layer (harbor#1149) with their own
# probe rows in <private>/inject.d/notes.tsv, and the suite reads those too when HARBOR_NOTES_PRIVATE names that
# layer. A layer that carries a pack with no row there fails the same way.
# FIXTURE PACKS. A pack in fixtures/inject/packs/<name>/ is never installed and names no real repo; it exists so the
# default run reaches an engine predicate that only the private layer's packs use (`cmd-contains`, with two `when:`
# lines stacked). Its rows say `<name>` in the pack column, and it is a tracked note like any other: no row, no pass.
# EVERY NOTE NEEDS A SILENT ARM TOO. CONSTITUTION §2.11 — a false positive is a
# defect, and a fixture that only ever asserts firing cannot see one. The silent
# arms here are near-misses on purpose (`<tool> run` without `--full-refresh`,
# `gh pr list` beside `gh pr create`, the phrase quoted in prose rather than run),
# because an absurd negative proves only that the predicate is not `true`.
# COLUMNS   pack · repo · id · arm · label · payload
#   pack    the context-rules/ scope the note ships in (`box` = user/); `self` = harbor's own context-rules/harbor/ (in the private layer's rows,
#           a folder of that layer's inject.d/); a name under fixtures/inject/packs/ is a fixture pack (above)
#   repo    the fixture repo shape: `plain`, `skills` (a HIDDEN skill), `visible`, or `naming` (carries
#           bin/lint-name.sh and standards/naming/, the only repos name-note judges)
#   arm     fire | silent | deny   (deny = a run: pack returning the decision sentinel)
#   payload one line of JSON. @REPO@ expands to the fixture repo, @OTHER@ to a
#           SECOND repo that carries packs, @BARE@ to a repo that carries none,
